newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE to switch wheat futures to afternoon trading.
newsitem.headline: SFE to switch wheat futures to afternoon trading.

text.p: The Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) will switch trading in its low-volume wheat contract from mornings to afternoons next week, an SFE spokesman told Reuters.
Wheat futures trading will take place between 2.00 p.m. and 4.00 p.m. (0400 and 0600 GMT) from August 11, he said.
As reported on Tuesday, the SFE is also considering changing trading in the wheat contract from floor pits to screens, with electronic matching of bids.
SFE wheat futures traded 6,482 contracts in calendar 1996, after trade began in March.
This compared with 9.2 million contracts traded in the biggest-selling contract, three year bonds.
The SFE's other agricultural commodity contract, wool, had 7,554 contracts traded in 1996.
